summary: Addressing class imbalance (class-weighting, random oversampling, or SMOTE) does not improve overall model quality on this dataset by ranking/balanced-error metrics (ROC-AUC and macro-F1 both stay flat or drop slightly) — instead it mainly re-shifts the decision threshold, trading a large gain in minority-class (>50K) recall for a comparable loss in minority-class precision. Since the imbalance here is only moderate (~76/24), the unweighted baseline was already competitive.
primary_metric_name: Macro-F1 difference (Random Forest, class_weight='balanced' minus baseline)
direction: baseline (no imbalance handling) >= imbalance-handled models on macro-F1 and ROC-AUC; imbalance handling substantially raises minority-class recall/balanced-accuracy at the cost of precision
methodological_choices: Target binarized (>50K=1). Categorical NaNs imputed as an explicit 'Missing' category then one-hot encoded; numeric features median-imputed and standardized. 80/20 stratified train/test split (test set held out for final confirmation only). Two model families compared (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, 300 trees) x four imbalance strategies (none/baseline, class_weight='balanced', random oversampling, SMOTE), all fit inside a pipeline with resampling applied only to training folds. Compared via 5-fold stratified CV on the training set using ROC-AUC, macro-F1, minority-class F1/recall, and balanced accuracy — macro-F1 was treated as the primary 'overall quality' metric since it penalizes both false positives and false negatives across both classes, unlike ROC-AUC (largely threshold/imbalance-insensitive) or minority recall alone (ignores precision cost).
verification_method: 5x repeated stratified 5-fold CV (25 folds total, seed=123) comparing Random Forest baseline vs class_weight='balanced' on the training set, plus an independent check on the untouched 20% held-out test set fit with seed=42.
verification_result: Held up: across all 25 repeated-CV folds, macro-F1 was lower with class_weight balancing in 100% of folds (mean diff = -0.0102, std = 0.0036, 95% CI [-0.0116, -0.0088], entirely below zero); ROC-AUC also dropped slightly but consistently (mean diff = -0.0011, std = 0.0008). The held-out test set replicated the same pattern and magnitude: macro-F1 0.8033 (baseline) vs 0.7885 (class_weight), ROC-AUC 0.9187 vs 0.9180, while minority recall rose from 0.620 to 0.843 and minority precision fell from 0.781 to 0.597. The direction and rough size of the effect were stable across both validation schemes.
